source.title: Kronecker Factorization Improves Efficiency and Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Vadim Kurochkin; Yaroslav Aksenov; Daniil Laptev; Daniil Gavrilov; Nikita Balagansky

record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE feature absorption and splitting, finding that KronSAE variants lower absorption metrics while maintaining a similar feature-splitting rate. This refines the claim about whether splitting is clean, but it does not test splitting across dictionary sizes.
record.gate_note: The direct results bearing on a claim version are the Gemma-2-2B absorption and feature-splitting metrics in Figure 10. The correlation-grouping, toy-covariance, interpretability, and geometry analyses do not test whether increasing dictionary size replaces a coarse feature with finer features that partition its inputs and lie near its direction.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes an SAE architecture (KronSAE). Its absorption analysis uses SAEBench absorption and split metrics as an evaluation benchmark for that method against TopK and Matryoshka baselines, at one dictionary size (F=2^14) on Gemma-2-2B. It reports no dictionary-size sweep of splitting and no test of whether absorption persists as size or sparsity changes. The text states only the relative result (Kron variants reduce absorption, with a similar split rate); all values are in Figure 10. The finding is a mitigation result for the study's own method, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, but secondary. The authors' main conclusion is that KronSAE matches TopK on the EV–FLOPs frontier with fewer encoder FLOPs and yields more interpretable, more specific latents. On absorption, Kron variants 'tend to reduce' partial and full absorption with a similar split rate. The authors hypothesize this comes from the AND-like gating and head partitioning.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a Kronecker-factorized encoder and Matryoshka combinations against standard TopK SAE; its absorption analysis fixes dictionary size and varies sparsity rather than comparing SAEs of increasing dictionary size.
record.method_sensitivity: The absorption analysis varies ℓ0 across 8, 16, 32, and 64; the authors report the same qualitative pattern across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: KronSAE variants (an encoder AND-like co-activation prior) tend to lower mean absorption fraction and full-absorption score vs TopK across ℓ0 8–64 at F=2^14. Their split rate is similar to TopK.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural encoder priors (factorized heads with AND-like composition) reduce, but do not eliminate, feature absorption without changing split rate.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The direct absorption results are presented in a figure without exact values or stated uncertainty. The test uses Gemma-2-2B at one dictionary size and does not directly measure parent-child input coverage.

untested.parts: No dictionary-size sweep of coarse-to-fine splitting, input coverage, or directional proximity.
No test of size-driven splitting in large models or open SAE releases.
No test of nested split families mirroring a concept hierarchy. Kron head clustering is an architectural prior, not split-feature families.
No parent/child firing analysis. Absorption is not compared across dictionary sizes, and the TopK baseline's trend across ℓ0 is not stated in text.
No cross-size latent decomposition or novel-latent analysis.
Matryoshka and TopK absorption and split metrics are plotted, but the text states no Matryoshka-vs-TopK result.

missing.what: TopK baseline absorption fraction and full-absorption scores at ℓ0 8, 16, 32 and 64. These show whether absorption persists across sparsity in a 2B model.
Matryoshka-512/1024 vs TopK absorption and split metrics, an objective change compared with the standard TopK objective.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T5/tests is overstated. All absorption numbers are figure-only, and the only stated result is a relative improvement of the authors' own method. Appendix G's remark that fine-grained architectures 'may exhibit' splitting or absorption is speculative, with no measurement. The record's rows also omit the Matryoshka baselines included in Figure 10.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of dictionary size measuring replacement of coarse features by finer features, input coverage, or directional proximity.
No tests of the claimed size-scaling pattern in large models or open SAE releases.
No test that split-feature families are nested, geometrically close, and mirror a model concept hierarchy.
Does not directly measure whether a parent fails to fire on inputs where a specific child fires; does not vary dictionary size.
No comparison of larger-SAE latents as combinations of smaller-SAE latents or a test for novel latents across dictionary sizes.
No comparison isolating the sparsity objective as the cause of splitting, and no test of whether Matryoshka SAEs reduce splitting as an objective artifact.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Absorption and split metrics serve as an evaluation axis for the authors' architecture. The paper does not test whether splitting or absorption occurs as any version states.

tranche.reason: Section 6.1 uses SAEBench absorption and split metrics to evaluate the authors' own KronSAE against TopK and Matryoshka at one size, F=2^14. It runs no size sweep. The text states no TopK-only trend across sparsity and no Matryoshka-vs-TopK split result, so it does not test V1-V6. The reader's T5 call is not supported.

source_check.notes: All 12 rows compare the study's own method (KronSAE) with TopK and Matryoshka baselines. Values exist only in the Figure 10 plots. The text says only that Kron variants 'tend to reduce' absorption and full absorption, with a 'similar rate of feature splitting'. Gemma-2-2B, F=2^14, l0 in {8,16,32,64}. Section 6.1 does not state the layer (other comparisons use layer 12). The rows carry no verdict weight.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: KronSAE variants compared with TopK SAE across ℓ0 values 8, 16, 32, and 64
reader_labels.reason: Absorption and full-absorption scores tend to be lower, but the reported feature-splitting rate remains similar; the findings qualify the extent to which absorption accompanies splitting (r1–r12).
